summary: This roadmap develops geometric Enriques surfaces over arbitrary fields and flat proper algebraic-space families, their canonical degree-two covers, characteristic-two types and numerical lattices. It combines Picard descent, dyadic twisting, finite-field genus-one fibrations and lattice configuration arguments to plan integral and F₂ nonexistence. The endpoints retain explicit completeness, omitted-configuration and source-acquisition gates rather than claiming that these gaps are proved.

nodes.title: Enriques surface
nodes.statement: For a field k and a smooth proper k-scheme Y of pure dimension two, IsEnriques(Y/k) means that Y over an algebraic closure has H⁰(O)=k̄, canonical line bundle numerically trivial and ℓ-adic second Betti number 10, for one (equivalently every) prime ℓ different from char(k). This is a geometric predicate on the existing surface, with no perfection or characteristic restriction.
hypotheses: k is an arbitrary field; Y/k is smooth and proper of pure dimension two. No Enriques hypothesis is assumed in defining the predicate.
The Betti prime ℓ is different from char(k); the conjunction is imposed after algebraic closure.
proofSteps: Use smoothness and properness on the native scheme map; request cohomology, numerical triviality and ℓ-independence from the indicated suppliers. Prove closure-independent formulation before exporting it.
acceptance: Keep the stated field, multiplicity and Picard hypotheses; give the proof on the actual geometric objects.

It has its canonical zero-section. This construction is an Enriques adapter to the shared genus-one Jacobian construction.
hypotheses: k is any field; Y/k is geometrically Enriques and φ:Y→P¹_k is a genus-one fibration, elliptic or quasielliptic.
The shared genus-one supplier provides generic Pic⁰, its regular compactification when necessary, and the relatively minimal regular surface model.
proofSteps: Import generic Pic⁰ and its minimal regular model from the proposed genus-one supplier, including the unpointed genus-one torsor and regular nonsmooth quasielliptic cases. JacobianChallenge supplies shared relative-Picard sheaf foundations and the smooth pointed constructor where a point has been obtained, not a general quasielliptic surface Jacobian.
acceptance: Keep the stated field, multiplicity and Picard hypotheses; give the proof on the actual geometric objects.

nodes.statement: At a simple fibre of that elliptic fibration, the Jacobian fibre and Enriques fibre are isomorphic over the residue field.

proofSteps: Find a point of the smooth locus of the whole scheme fibre. For tree additive types choose a multiplicity-one terminal component; for I_n cycles remove at most two intersection points from a split P¹; for type IV remove its single triple-intersection point. Treat nonsplit I₁/I₂ by their normalization/conductor descriptions. Do not use the regular locus of the reduction when the scheme fibre has thicker components.

Lift that smooth point over the Henselian local base, trivialize the generic torsor and invoke uniqueness of the minimal regular model. This supplies the residue-field isomorphism, not only equal geometric type.

nodes.title: Descent of all Mordell–Weil sections
nodes.statement: Every geometric Mordell–Weil section of the Jacobian of a constant-full-Picard Enriques elliptic fibration over F₂ is defined over F₂. Thus MW(J/P¹)=MW(J_F̄₂/P¹_F̄₂) under base change.
hypotheses: Y/F₂ is an Enriques surface with constant full relative Picard group scheme (Z¹⁰⊕Z/2)_{F₂}.
φ:Y→P¹_{F₂} is an elliptic fibration, and J→P¹_{F₂} is its relatively minimal regular Jacobian with zero-section.
proofSteps: Over F̄₂(t), Tsen kills the Brauer obstruction to Picard points being line bundles. Restriction from geometric Pic(Y) to the generic curve is surjective; subtract degree/2 times a descended two-section R to obtain the Galois-equivariant surjection to Pic⁰, hence MW.
Constant full Picard makes this quotient action trivial; Galois-fixed points of J(F̄₂(t)) descend to J(F₂(t)). Br(F₂(t)) is not claimed zero, and the square-zero two-section case is retained.
acceptance: Tsen is used over F̄₂(t) only; no line-bundle descent over F₂(t) is inferred from it.

The list asserts necessary possibilities, not existence of any Enriques realization. Here E_n denotes the smooth F₂ elliptic curve with n rational points; Ĩ_n denotes a nonsplit semistable fibre. The triple is considered up to permutation.
